label: Candidate Guides
content: import { DocsLayout } from "components"; import { getEmbedConfig } from "utils/constants"; import { CandidateGuideEmbed } from "components/CandidateGuideEmbed/CandidateGuideEmbed"; # Candidate Guides ## Efficiently create and present candidate Q&A's, helping audiences learn more about elections. With Populist, organizations can streamline the process of creating candidate guides for many elections at a time. Simply create the questions you'd like to ask the candidates and select the races they are in, and our platform will generate forms, URLs, and embeddable guides that will automatically update with the candidates' responses once they are received. Our civic database includes candidate contact information so it's easy to export and send questions to candidates using your favorite email list software. ### Overview When you create a new candidate guide, you are actually creating a new group of candidate guides that all have the same questions. This allows you to create a bulk number of candidate guides with the same questions. We will refer to these groups as candidate guide groups, and the guides for each race in a group as candidate guides. ### Create Your Questions Once you create a new candidate guide group, you can add questions that you want to ask candidates, with the following options. #### Tags - Tag your question with the most relevant issues so responses can be best searched and categorized. #### Character limit - Limit candidate responses to a number of characters. #### Placeholder text - Placeholder text is the copy that is shown in the input field when it is empty - this can be used to give additional context for candidates answering a question. ### Selecting Races Next, add the races with the candidates that you want to ask questions to. Each added race creates a new candidate guide for that race. You can search and filter races in an election with the following options. #### Election year - Select the year of the election that you're searching for races in. #### Race type - Choose whether you're searching for primary or general races. #### State - Select the state that you're searching for races in. #### Scope - Filter search results by Federal, State, or Local races. A Federal race example includes races for U.S. Senate offices, while State races include Governor, Secretary of State, or state legislature offices. Local races are county or further downballot offices like city council or school boards. If you're asking the same questions to candidates across multiple races, simply add each race to the candidate guide group and they will appear under Races. ### Managing Guides Under Races you'll see all the races that have been added to the candidate guide group. You'll see the following helpful information in the table of races: #### Name - The title of the race, which includes information like the state, office, municipality, race type, and year. #### County - The name of the county that the race is in. This helps to further distinguish races. #### Candidates - The number of candidates in a race. #### Submissions - The number of responses that candidates have submitted. #### Date Added - The date that the race was added to the candidate guide group. #### Emails Sent - A checkbox to help you manually track whether an email was sent to the candidates in a race. By clicking on a row in the Races table, you'll be able to access each race's candidate guide management page. On this page you'll find the following information: #### Candidate Table - A table of all the candidates in the race. In this table you can edit a candidate's email and phone number, and also directly access the URL to the candidate's personalized form that is used to respond to the questions in the candidate guide. #### Configuration Options - Manually set the fixed height of the candidate guide embeds, as well as the default language of the guide. #### Preview - See what the candidate guide embed will look like on a website, with all candidate submissions. #### Embed Code - This is the actual code needed to embed each candidate guide onto a website. #### Public Preview Link - A URL to a preview of the candidate guide that can be publicly shared. #### Deployments - URLs where the candidate guide has been embedded. ### Sending Questions Once questions and races are added to a candidate guide group, you can export out a spreadsheet of all the candidates in the guide group that includes the following columns: #### Race Title - The title of the race that the candidate is running in. The title includes information like the state, office, municipality, race type, and year. #### First Name - The first name of the candidate. #### Middle Name - The middle name of the candidate. #### Last Name - The last name of the candidate. #### Preferred Name - The preferred name of the candidate. #### Suffix - Any suffix in a candidate's name e.g. Jr, III, Esq. #### Full Name - The full name of the candidate that includes the first, middle, last, suffix, and preferred names. #### Email - The candidate's email. #### Form Link - The URL to the automatically generated form that the candidate can use to submit their responses. #### Was Candidate Emailed - Either a true or false value based on the "Email Sent" checkbox that is manually set by users to track whether an email was sent. #### Last Submission - The date and time of the last submission by the candidate. Use this exported spreadsheet with your preferred email list management software to send emails to each of the candidates. Using each column in the spreadsheet, you can personalize the emails to include the candidate's name and the link they will use to respond to the guide questions. ### Managing Submissions You can access each candidate's submissions by clicking on the Submissions tab at the top of the candidate guide management page. To see responses to each question, click on a question and the submissions will populate in the Responses table below. From this table you can add translations, editorial, and manage duplicate submissions for similar guides. export default function DocsCandidateGuides({ children }) { return {children}; }

label: Legislation
content: import { DocsLayout } from "components"; import { getEmbedConfig } from "utils/constants"; import { BillWidget } from "components/BillWidget/BillWidget"; # Legislation ## Keep audiences up-to-date on the latest legislation. Legislation embeds give the latest information about bills as they move through the legislature. They help audiences easily understand what the legislation is about, who is involved, and where the bill is currently in the process of becoming law. Legislation embeds also capture engagement by allowing audiences to vote on whether they support, oppose, or are undecided on a bill. Below are the types of information on each legislation embed: ### Name The name of the legislation. This is AI-generated and edited by the Populist staff. ### Code This is the legislation's government code that is used to identify it. ### Year This is the year that the legislation was introduced. ### Issue Tags Issue tags offer a quick way to show the subject matter of legislation through our categories. ### Summary These summaries are AI-generated and reviewed by Populist staff to make sure they are accurate and representative. ### Full Text Link If audiences want to dive deeper, we provide links to the full text of legislation on the official government website. ### Status The status area shows where a bill is in the process of becoming law. ### Latest votes If legislation has been voted on in one or both chambers, the latest vote totals will be shown here. ### Sponsors The sponsors section shows the partisan breakdown of the authors of a bill. ### Public voting Public voting is a way to gauge sentiment on legislation. Audiences can share whether they support, oppose, or are undecided on legislation, and see how others have responded. Public voting can be configured either to allow anonymous responses, or to require names and emails that are only shared with the organization. export default function DocsLegislation({ children }) { return {children}; }

label: What is a conversation?
content:
import { DocsLayout } from "components";

## What is a Conversation?

Populist's **Conversations** is an open-source platform that helps large groups share and understand their collective views. It is an implementation of a [Wikisurvey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wiki_survey) and inspired by other platforms including [Pol.is](https://pol.is) with a few key improvements.

When using Populist conversations, people write short comments and then vote on other people's comments by selecting support, oppose, or neutral. The system shows comments to voters in a semi-random way to ensure broad exposure of ideas.

What makes this different from regular surveys:

- Participants create the content themselves instead of answering preset questions
- People can contribute meaningfully without having to vote on everything
- The system works efficiently even with hundreds, thousands, or potentially millions of participants

#### Participating in Conversations

Browse through the list of existing conversations to find topics that interest you. Click on a conversation to view the discussion and contribute your thoughts and opinions.

#### Managing Conversations

Organization administrators have the ability to manage conversations, including editing or deleting conversations as needed. This ensures that discussions remain relevant and appropriate for the organization.

Distribution
content:
import { DocsLayout, Divider } from "components";

## Distributing a Conversation

The conversation owner can distribute the conversation to participants using the following methods:

#### Direct Link

Share the conversation link with participants via email, social media, or other communication channels. Participants can access the conversation by clicking the link.

#### Embed Code

Embed the conversation on your website using the provided embed code. Participants can engage with the conversation directly on your website.

<Divider />

## Marketing

Promote the conversation to attract participants and increase engagement. Consider the following marketing strategies:

#### Email list

Send an email to your subscribers inviting them to participate in the conversation. Include a brief description of the conversation and a call-to-action to join.

#### Social media

Share the conversation link on your social media channels to reach a wider audience. Use engaging visuals and captions to attract participants.

#### Paid Ads

Consider running paid ads to promote the conversation to a targeted audience. Use platforms like Google Ads or Facebook Ads to reach potential participants.

export default function DocsConversationsDistribution({ children }) {
  return <DocsLayout currentPage="conversations">{children}</DocsLayout>;
}

label: Moderation
content:
import { DocsLayout } from "components";

## Moderation

The conversation owner controls moderation through the admin interface.
Each new comment can be approved, rejected, or left unmoderated. While
Conversations work without moderation, moderating effectively saves
participants' time by removing irrelevant content.

## Moderation Schemes

Strict Moderation (Default) Works like a whitelist Comments only appear
after moderator approval. Recommended when embedding on your website to
prevent inappropriate content. Permissive Moderation Works like a
blacklist Comments appear immediately Can be removed later by moderators
You can switch between these in the conversation's admin configuration.

export default function DocsConversationsModeration({ children }) {
  return <DocsLayout currentPage="conversations">{children}</DocsLayout>;
}

content:
import { Divider, DocsLayout, CodeBlock } from "components";

# API Reference

<Divider />
## Introducing: The Populist public API

The Populist public API provides access to the Populist platform's features and
data. You can use the API to consume data about elections, politicians, bills,
and more.

Populist supports two API styles:

- **GraphQL** for clients that need flexible queries across the complete data
  graph.
- **REST** for common datasets with stable, resource-oriented request and
  response contracts.

### GraphQL

Use GraphQL to request exactly the fields your application needs.

A query to the Populist API could looks something like this:

<CodeBlock
  code={`query {
    elections(filter: { state: CO }) {
      title
      description
      electionDate
    }
}`}
  language="graphql"
/>

### REST

The versioned REST API is available under `/api/v1`. Its first dataset endpoint
resolves races and ballot measures for a supplied address and election:

<CodeBlock
  code={`POST https://api.populist.us/api/v1/elections/YOUR_ELECTION_ID/ballot`}
  language="http"
/>

Start with the [REST overview](/docs/api/rest), then follow the complete
[ballot-by-address guide](/docs/api/ballot-by-address).

export default function DocsApiIntroduction({ children }) {
  return <DocsLayout currentPage="api">{children}</DocsLayout>;
}

import { DocsLayout } from "components";

# API Reference

<Divider />
## Authentication

Production API access requires an `Authorization` header containing the bearer
API key supplied during onboarding. This applies to both GraphQL and REST
requests:

```json
"Authorization": "Bearer YOUR_API_KEY"
```

If you do not have an API key, you can request one by contacting us at
[info@populist.us](mailto:info@populist.us)

Never put an API key in a browser bundle, URL, query parameter, or client-side
log. Browser applications should call the Populist API through a trusted
backend. Authentication and quota requirements can differ in development or
staging environments; use the base URL and credentials supplied for that
environment.

  return <DocsLayout currentPage="api">{children}</DocsLayout>;
}

label: REST Overview
content:
import { Divider, DocsLayout, CodeBlock } from "components";

export const restQuickstartExample = String.raw`curl --request GET \
  --url https://api.populist.us/api/v1/ \
  --header "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY" \
  --header "Accept: application/json"`;

export const restClientExample = [
  'const POPULIST_API_BASE_URL = "https://api.populist.us/api/v1";',
  "",
  "export class PopulistApiError extends Error {",
  "  constructor(problem, requestId) {",
  '    super(problem.detail || "Populist API request failed");',
  '    this.name = "PopulistApiError";',
  "    this.status = problem.status;",
  "    this.code = problem.code;",
  "    this.requestId = requestId;",
  "  }",
  "}",
  "",
  "export async function populistRequest(path, options = {}) {",
  "  const response = await fetch(POPULIST_API_BASE_URL + path, {",
  "    ...options,",
  "    headers: {",
  '      Accept: "application/json",',
  '      Authorization: "Bearer " + process.env.POPULIST_API_KEY,',
  '      "X-Request-Id": crypto.randomUUID(),',
  "      ...options.headers,",
  "    },",
  "  });",
  "",
  '  const requestId = response.headers.get("x-request-id");',
  "  const payload = await response.json();",
  "",
  "  if (!response.ok) {",
  "    throw new PopulistApiError(payload, requestId);",
  "  }",
  "",
  "  return { data: payload.data, requestId };",
  "}",
].join("\n");

# API Reference

<Divider />

## REST API

The Populist REST API provides stable, resource-oriented access to common
datasets. Use it when your integration does not need GraphQL's field-level query
control.

The production base URL is:

<CodeBlock code={`https://api.populist.us/api/v1`} language="http" />

Use the environment URL and bearer API key supplied during onboarding. All
examples below use production for clarity.

### Quickstart

Check API discovery and liveness:

<CodeBlock code={restQuickstartExample} language="bash" />

The API index advertises the currently available REST resources:

<CodeBlock
  code={`{
  "data": {
    "version": "v1",
    "health": "/api/v1/health",
    "states": "/api/v1/states",
    "ballotByAddress": "/api/v1/elections/{electionId}/ballot"
  }
}`}
  language="json"
/>

### A small JavaScript client

Keep credentials on your server. This helper adds the standard headers,
preserves the response request ID, and turns problem responses into typed
errors:

<CodeBlock code={restClientExample} language="javascript" />

Use this helper from a backend, serverless function, or another trusted runtime.
Do not expose `POPULIST_API_KEY` through a `NEXT_PUBLIC_` environment variable.

### Successful responses

Dataset endpoints use a top-level `data` envelope. Collection endpoints can
also include `meta` pagination information.

Every REST response includes `X-Request-Id`. Send your own opaque value, or let
Populist generate one. Keep that ID in application telemetry because it is the
best value to provide when troubleshooting. Do not put an address, email, token,
or other personal data in it.

### Errors

REST errors use `application/problem+json` with a stable machine-readable
`code`:

<CodeBlock
  code={`{
  "type": "about:blank",
  "title": "Unprocessable Entity",
  "status": 422,
  "code": "invalid_address",
  "detail": "The address could not be resolved to a voting location.",
  "instance": "/api/v1/elections/7f7f1111-2222-4333-8444-555555555555/ballot"
}`}
  language="json"
/>

Branch on the HTTP status and `code`, not the human-readable `title` or
`detail`. Correct 400, 404, 405, 413, 415, and 422 responses before trying
again. Retry 429, 503, and 504 responses only with a bounded exponential
backoff and jitter. Honor `Retry-After` when it is present.

### HTTP conventions

- Send and accept JSON with `Content-Type: application/json` and
  `Accept: application/json`.
- Treat IDs as opaque UUID strings.
- Ignore response fields your client does not recognize.
- Handle new enum values defensively.
- Do not use titles or slugs as stable identity.
- Use HTTPS for every request.
- Do not cache responses marked `Cache-Control: no-store`.

### Versioning

The major API version is part of the path. Breaking changes require a new major
path such as `/api/v2`. Additive fields and enum values can be introduced
within v1, so clients should be tolerant readers.

### Available datasets

- [Ballot by Address](/docs/api/ballot-by-address): resolve election, race,
  candidate, result, and ballot-measure data for a US address.

The machine-readable contract is available as
[OpenAPI 3.1](/openapi/rest-v1.yaml).

  return <DocsLayout currentPage="api">{children}</DocsLayout>;
}

label: Ballot by Address
content: import { Divider, DocsLayout, CodeBlock, DocsTable } from "components"; export const ballotCurlExample = String.raw`curl --request POST \ --url https://api.populist.us/api/v1/elections/7f7f1111-2222-4333-8444-555555555555/ballot \ --header "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY" \ --header "Content-Type: application/json" \ --header "X-Request-Id: client-request-123" \ --data '{ "address": { "line1": "123 Main St", "city": "Minneapolis", "state": "MN", "postalCode": "55401", "country": "US" } }'`; export const ballotClientExample = [ 'const electionId = "7f7f1111-2222-4333-8444-555555555555";', "", "const result = await populistRequest(", ' "/elections/" + electionId + "/ballot",', " {", ' method: "POST",', ' headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" },', " body: JSON.stringify({", " address: {", ' line1: "123 Main St",', ' city: "Minneapolis",', ' state: "MN",', ' postalCode: "55401",', ' country: "US",', " },", " }),", " }", ");", "", "console.log(result.data.coverage);", "console.log(result.data.races);", "console.log(result.data.ballotMeasures);", ].join("\n"); # API Reference ## Ballot by Address Resolve Populist's races and ballot measures for a US voting address in a specific election. This endpoint returns informational election data. It is not an official sample ballot, voter-registration check, polling-place lookup, or statement of voter eligibility. Direct users to the relevant election authority for official information. ### Endpoint You need an election UUID before making this request. The endpoint does not discover elections. Obtain the configured election ID, environment base URL, and bearer API key during onboarding. ### Request Using the helper from the [REST overview](/docs/api/rest): The JSON body is limited to 8 KiB. Unknown JSON fields and unknown query parameters are rejected. address.line1, "Yes", "Non-empty after trimming; at most 200 characters; no control characters.", ], [ address.line2, "No", "At most 200 characters. Accepted for compatibility, but deliberately not used for district resolution, sent to geocoding, or stored.", ], [ address.city, "Yes", "Non-empty after trimming; at most 100 characters; no control characters.", ], [ address.state, "Yes", "Valid two-letter US state or territory code, case-insensitive.", ], [address.postalCode, "Yes", "Five-digit ZIP or ZIP+4."], [ address.country, "No", "US or USA, case-insensitive. Defaults to US.", ], ]} /> Caller-provided coordinates and legislative districts are rejected. Populist derives them from the address. ### Filter candidates by endorsement Add `endorserId` as an optional organization UUID: This filters each race's `candidates` array to candidates endorsed by the organization. It does not remove races, ballot measures, result totals, or winner references. A race can therefore remain present with an empty `candidates` array. ### Response An abridged success response looks like this: The complete response schema is available in the [OpenAPI contract](/openapi/rest-v1.yaml). #### Election `election` contains the stable ID, slug, title, optional description, optional state, and `YYYY-MM-DD` election date. #### Races Each race contains identity and election fields, the office, running candidates, reported results, and public related embeds. - `raceType` is `primary` or `general`. - `voteType` is `plurality` or `rankedchoice`. - `office.electionScope` is `national`, `state`, `county`, `city`, or `district`. - `office.politicalScope` is `local`, `state`, or `federal`. - Candidate and incumbent party, contact, image, and asset fields can be `null`. - Result counts and percentages can be `null` until results are available. Percentages are percentage points rounded to one decimal place. - `winners` can be empty before a race is called. - Administrative embed-origin restrictions are never exposed. #### Ballot measures Each measure contains its ID, title, optional description, state, measure code, nullable vote and precinct counts, and nullable election scope. ### Geographic coverage Always inspect `data.coverage` before presenting the response as an address-specific ballot. address_specific, address_specific], ["Texas", address_specific, statewide_only], [ "Other supported state or territory", statewide_only, statewide_only, ], ]} /> `statewide_only` means district and local matching is unavailable. It does not guarantee that every statewide record is present. Display or otherwise handle `coverage.warnings`; branch on the stable coverage values rather than warning text. ### Ordering Arrays have deterministic ordering: - Races use office priority, district, seat, title, and ID. - Candidates and incumbents use last name, first name, and ID. - Candidate vote rows and related embeds use ID. - Ballot measures use title and ID. Do not use this ordering as a synchronization cursor. ### Errors and retries invalid_path_parameter, invalid_parameter, malformed_query, invalid_body , "Correct the request.", ], ["404", resource_not_found, "The election does not exist."], ["405", method_not_allowed, "Use POST."], ["413", payload_too_large, "Reduce the request below 8 KiB."], [ "415", unsupported_media_type, "Send Content-Type: application/json.", ], [ "422", invalid_address, "Ask the user to review the address; do not retry unchanged input.", ], ["429", rate_limited, "Retry after Retry-After with jitter."], [ "500", internal_error, "Retry cautiously and report persistent failures.", ], [ "503", address_service_unavailable, "Retry after Retry-After with jitter.", ], [ "504", request_timeout, "Retry once with jitter and report persistent failures.", ], ]} /> Keep retries bounded. Include the response `X-Request-Id`, election ID, environment, timestamp, status, and problem code in support reports. Do not include the full voter address unless an approved support channel explicitly requires it. ### Address privacy Use HTTPS and prevent application and proxy logs from recording request bodies. The address is never returned. `line2` is discarded during validation. An exact cached address can be reused without geocoding. On a cache miss, street, city, state, and ZIP are sent to the configured geocoding service to derive coordinates and districts. A temporary address record is used during selection and Populist attempts to remove newly created records after processing when they are not connected to a user profile. Abnormal termination or cleanup failure can interrupt that best-effort removal. Confirm contractual retention, subprocessors, and deletion requirements during onboarding before sending production personal data. ### Client checklist - Keep the API key in a trusted backend. - Test a known Minnesota address and verify both coverage fields. - Test invalid JSON, invalid ZIP, unknown election, and unresolvable address. - Ensure request and response logs do not contain the address. - Propagate `X-Request-Id` without personal data. - Implement bounded 429, 503, and 504 retries with jitter. - Decide how empty candidate, race, and ballot-measure arrays display. - Describe the result as informational rather than an official ballot. export default function DocsApiBallotByAddress({ children }) { return {children}; }

label: String
content: The `String` scalar type represents textual data, represented as UTF-8 character sequences. The String type is most often used by GraphQL to represent free-form human-readable text.

label: ID
content: The `ID` scalar type represents a unique identifier, often used to refetch an object or as key for a cache. The ID type appears in a JSON response as a String; however, it is not intended to be human-readable. When expected as an input type, any string (such as `"4"`) or integer (such as `4`) input value will be accepted as an ID.

label: Int
content: The `Int` scalar type represents non-fractional signed whole numeric values. Int can represent values between -(2^31) and 2^31 - 1.

label: Boolean
content: The `Boolean` scalar type represents `true` or `false`.

label: Float
content: The `Float` scalar type represents signed double-precision fractional values as specified by [IEEE 754](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IEEE_floating_point).

label: DateTime
content:
Implement the DateTime<Utc> scalar

The input/output is a string in RFC3339 format.

label: UUID

A UUID is a unique 128-bit number, stored as 16 octets. UUIDs are parsed as
Strings within GraphQL. UUIDs are used to assign unique identifiers to
entities without requiring a central allocating authority.
